comment: One row per environment name the scan of scripts/scan-env-names.sh yields. `class` is the allowlist class a name keeps, `toggle` a name that becomes a config key, or `drop` a name with no reader anywhere. `key` is the config key for the toggle and behavior-override classes. `reader` is derived composition-aware: a name reached as os.getenv(f'MEOWKIT_{suffix}') is recorded as read, because a literal-name grep reports it as reader-less. This file is the allowlist the environment-read check loads; it lives at the repository root, outside every scanned tree, so a dropped name's own row cannot keep that name in the universe. The reader column is checked in both directions by scripts/check-env-reads.cjs: a live name must be read at the file named here, and a replaced name must be read nowhere.

classes.credential: a secret. Never a config key, because a committed file must not hold one.
classes.host: supplied by the host process (CLAUDE_*). Outside this prefix set.
classes.safety-path: read by a safety entrypoint. Never a config key: the committed file stays unreachable from those paths.
classes.runtime-handoff: a per-invocation value one process writes and the next reads. A committed file cannot carry it.
classes.skill-option: read only by one skill's own scripts, several of them Python, which must not need a YAML parser.
classes.behavior-override: has a config key and stays readable from the environment at the top of the precedence chain, because losing it silently would turn an enforcement mode off.
classes.toggle: a user preference with a code reader. Becomes the config key in `key`.
classes.drop: no reader anywhere. Deleted from docs, agents, skills and settings; a still-exported one is a doctor finding.

compositionZones.why: env_utils.py composes the prefix with a suffix supplied by provider_router.py, so a literal-name scan sees none of these reads

nonSuffixLiterals.comment: Upper-case literals inside a composition zone that are NOT environment-name suffixes. Listed by name so a newly composed suffix is a violation rather than silently tolerated.
nonSuffixLiterals.RESOURCE_EXHAUSTED: a Gemini error status compared against

readerUnverifiable.comment: A read no syntactic scan can see. The reader column is still required to name a file that exists, so a renamed or deleted reader is caught; what is waived is only the proof that the read is in it.
readerUnverifiable.MEOWKIT_EVAL_SLUG: read by a markdown skill step, not by code: the step exports it in one shell block and reads it back in another
readerUnverifiable.MEOWKIT_GEMINI_API_KEY_2: the suffix index is composed at the call site (an f-string loop), so the name is spelled nowhere
readerUnverifiable.MEOWKIT_GEMINI_API_KEY_3: the suffix index is composed at the call site (an f-string loop), so the name is spelled nowhere
readerUnverifiable.MEOWKIT_GEMINI_API_KEY_4: the suffix index is composed at the call site (an f-string loop), so the name is spelled nowhere

removalExempt.comment: A name whose class is `toggle` or `drop` is a removed environment variable: a shell still exporting it is told so by `mewkit doctor`, with the key that replaced it or the fact that nothing replaced it. These names are exempt from that finding, because exporting them is not a stale export.
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_PM_AUTO: still honored — by agent prose rather than by code, so there is nothing stale about exporting it
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_TOKEN: not an environment variable: a module-level compiled regex whose identifier matches the scan regex
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_INTERNAL_DIRS: not an environment variable: an exported module constant whose identifier matches the scan regex
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_INTERNAL_FILES: not an environment variable: an exported module constant whose identifier matches the scan regex
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_CONFIG: never shipped as a setting; named only in the assertion that the workflow-config reader does not consult it
removalExempt.MEOWKIT_API_KEY: never a shipped setting: a fixture name from a deleted dotenv-parser self-check, surviving only in an archived changelog

retainedDropOccurrences.comment: A name in the `drop` class is deleted from docs, agents, skills and settings. These are the occurrences that deliberately survive, each with the file substring it may appear in and why. Any OTHER occurrence of a dropped name fails the universe test, so the deletion is enforced rather than hoped for, and a retained one cannot quietly spread to a new file.

MEOWKIT_CONFIG.why: named only in an assertion that the workflow-config reader does NOT consult it; deleting the mention would delete the proof

MEOWKIT_HARNESS_MODE.why: an archived changelog is a historical record — the same reason the scan places RELEASING.md out of scope; rewriting it would falsify what a past release shipped

MEOWKIT_INTERNAL_DIRS.why: not an environment name — an exported module constant whose identifier happens to match the scan regex

MEOWKIT_INTERNAL_FILES.why: not an environment name — an exported module constant whose identifier happens to match the scan regex

MEOWKIT_PM_AUTO.why: the opt-out an agent reads for itself: no code reader and no schema key, documented prose-only, which is the standing decision for this name. Deleting it would remove a user opt-out with nothing replacing it. The provider projections mirror the same prose, so the name is as live there as it is under .claude/

MEOWKIT_SUMMARY_MODE.why: an archived changelog is a historical record

MEOWKIT_TOKEN.why: not an environment name — a module-level compiled regex whose identifier happens to match the scan regex

MEOW_JIRA_BASE_URL.why: an archived changelog is a historical record; every live mention was repointed at MEOW_JIRA_SITE_URL, the name the Jira wrapper actually requires

MEOW_PROFILE.why: named only in assertions that no hook reads it; deleting the mention would delete the proof the removal landed

MEOWKIT_API_KEY.why: a fixture name from a deleted dotenv-parser self-check; an archived changelog is a historical record, the same reason the scan places RELEASING.md out of scope
